devin: Quick cost check I ran for dedicated inference pools — APAC (asia-southeast1) vs SFO (us-west1). Surprising delta once you add network egress + local SSDs + prem support. TL;DR: SFO looks cheaper for high-throughput, low-latency workloads; APAC only wins if traffic residency + low inter-region egress are required.

ashwin: can you paste the calc? :eyes:

devin: sure — boiled down to an effective "cost per 1M tokens" for our g5-like instance profile. Rough snippet: 
```
region, gpu_hour, reserved_discount, egress_per_gb, ssd_monthly, effective_cost_per_1M_tokens
us-west1, 3.20, 0.28, 0.12, 80, $18.5
asia-southeast1, 3.60, 0.20, 0.45, 95, $25.7
```
Notes: reserved_discount = committed use across 1yr we modeled; egress per GB is cloud provider list w/ regional premium. Effective cost includes token throughput uplift from local SSD cache (KV cache) assumptions.

matt: those egress numbers look rough — did you include inter-zone replication for autoscaler? that adds ~0.02/gb extra and some writes.

devin: yes — added replication and k8s control-plane egress. Also accounted for burst capacity (we'd keep spot in same region for burst). Biggest driver is network egress in APAC -> global endpoints + no cheap peer for our S3 backup + higher managed k8s node premium.

leah: what about latency-sensitive features? some product teams need <50ms tail. APAC->SFO RTT kills that. If we keep model ops in SFO but traffic from SG/HK, we'll need edge routing + streaming from SFO which may break SLAs.

ashwin: can we do a hybrid? model replicas in APAC for low-latency small traffic, and big throughput batches in SFO? how does that affect committed spend?

devin: hybrid viable. tradeoffs: commits are regional SKUs. If we split commit between regions we lose volume discount threshold. Modeled scenario: 60% capacity commit in SFO + 40% in APAC => effective blended price ~ $20.9/1M tokens (vs $18.5 all-in SFO). Still beats APAC-only but higher ops complexity and more headroom to manage rollouts.

matt: also consider procurement constraints — some GPU families limited in APAC. committing there might force older SKUs or higher MSRP.

leah: compliance asks: some customers require data to never leave APAC. for those we must host full stack in APAC even if more expensive. we should flag those customers and not route them to SFO.

devin: agreed. next steps: 1) create a small RFC with the blended commit numbers + expected savings vs ops cost and complexity, 2) run a 2-week canary placing a small 5-node reserved pool in APAC to validate perf + network costs in prod trace, 3) tag customers with residency reqs so router policies avoid cross-region egress.

ashwin: please include a sensitivity table for 6mo vs 1yr vs 3yr commits — provider discounts shift a lot. also include egress-optimized pathways (peerings, CDN for embeddings) in the model.

sre-bot: cluster-health report for us-west1: GPU reserved pools: capacity 64, used 49 (76%), avg tail latency 38ms, pod restarts 0.6/day. asia-southeast1: GPU reserved pools: capacity 32, used 29 (91%), avg tail latency 44ms, pod restarts 1.4/day.

billing-bot: Posted provisional billing delta calc: https://billing.internal.redwood/commits/1768123456 — includes egress estimates and committed discounts.

matt: ok — if you post the RFC I'll 👍. we should also loop in finance to validate the blended commit accounting (how we amortize commit fees across customers).

devin: will draft RFC today and ping finance + product. thanks all. :thumbsup:
